# Feature: Recovery as Declarative Data

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-034
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_interaction_wave2.md`

Collapse the six nested recovery layers that sit between an agent tool call and a keystroke into **one runner executing one declarative escalation plan per interaction family**, so that adding a fallback is an edit to a list of rungs rather than another wrapper around the action being retried.

**Why this is worth the risk.** Today six independently principled layers each own a slice of recovery, and none of them can see the others:

| #   | Layer                 | Location                                                                                                                | What it owns                                                                          |
| --- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `driveWithRetry`      | `packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-element.ts:365-443`                                                  | Re-resolve the field and drive again when the page re-mounted the form                |
| 2   | `withAttempts`        | `packages/core/src/interaction/attempt.ts:137-186`                                                                      | The generic bounded loop, its ledger, and `classifyFailure`                           |
| 3   | Engine re-acquisition | `packages/core/src/fill/engine.ts` — `MAX_REACQUISITIONS = 4`, `fieldHealingPort`, `driveWithFallback`, `withOpenProbe` | Stale-ref healing, driver-confidence fallback, the open-probe stage                   |
| 4   | The typing ladder     | `packages/core/src/interaction/typing.ts:commitText` + `mergeLedger`                                                    | Three HOW mechanisms and Wave 1's WHERE rung, spliced together afterwards             |
| 5   | The reaction watcher  | `packages/core/src/fill/react.ts:watchAndSelect`                                                                        | Post-typing popup watch and selection, now also the combobox driver's selection stage |
| 6   | Click retry           | `packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-click.ts:130-176`                                                         | A **second, separate** `withAttempts` with its own `CLICK_RECOVERY_BUDGET_MS`         |

The consequences are measured in `plan_interaction_wave2.md` §11 and in FEAT-031's evidence table. Nobody charges every action against one counter, so a rung can under-report its cost — `engine.ts` increments `actions` by `entered.ledger.records.length`, which counts _rungs_, not pointer or key operations. Nobody checks whether the remaining budget can cover a rung before starting it, so a failing fill answers in **8.7–13.9 s**: it starts work it cannot finish and is cut off. And each new failure class has arrived as another nesting level, which is exactly what memory forbids ("a new fallback is a plan edit, never a nested wrapper or an inline branch inside the action being retried").

**After this feature:** one `runEscalationPlan` owns eligibility, budgets, and the ledger. A plan is an ordered list of typed rungs — axis, evidence-based entry condition, cost cap, evidence produced — that can be read, tested, and reordered as data. A failing fill answers in **≤ 4 s** because entry conditions make fast-fail systematic rather than one hand-placed exit. The ledger becomes a projection of the executed plan, and "why did this rung run?" and "which axis spent the budget?" are answerable from `tool-calls.jsonl`.

### The three phases, and why they are separate

Plan §7 is explicit that "zero behavior change" and "one runner owns budgets" cannot be the same step. TASK-001 through TASK-012 map onto three phases; the phase boundary is what makes a regression attributable.

- **Phase 1 — Characterize before changing (TASK-001).** Freeze public outcomes, ordered low-level actions, elapsed/deadline behavior, and legacy ledgers at the protocol seam **and** the complete agent-tool seam. The 17-fixture gauntlet plus the adapter contract matrices are the entry gate; this feature may not begin until they pass.
- **Phase 2 — Migrate control flow in slices (TASK-002 … TASK-009).** Introduce the runner, migrate the typing/WHERE ladder and combobox **first** (combobox proves the runner because it exercises all three axes in one plan), then date, option, top-level fill re-resolution, and click retry. **Semantic and action-order assertions stay unedited throughout.** No migrated operation may call a nested retry runner; a rung body may run a **sub-plan through the same runner on the same budget and ledger**, which is what structurally removes `mergeLedger` and `mergedAttempts`.
- **Phase 3 — Activate single-owner accounting as a named behavior change (TASK-010 … TASK-012).** The runner checks the entry condition _and_ the remaining declared cap before starting a rung, and a wrapped port charges actual pointer/key/scroll actions so a rung cannot under-report cost. Budget-boundary expectations may change **only** here and are enumerated one by one; ordinary semantic outcomes and action ordering stay fixed. The verdict ledger lands here with its backward-compatible readers.

### Non-negotiable constraints

- **Dependency direction** (memory → Project Structure, plan §5). `driveWithRetry` lives in `packages/agent`, the other layers in `packages/core`, and **`packages/core` must never import `@yantra/agent`**. The resolution: `packages/core` exports one generic runner and plan type; the agent tool **declares an operation plan whose rungs call injected core operations**. `browser-click.ts` uses the same runner with a click plan. `packages/core/tests/boundary-rules.spec.ts` already proves the direction.
- **Finite protocol choreography inside a rung remains business logic** (plan §4). Calendar paging, popup settling/polling, candidate ranking, and dismissal stay inside the rung that performs them. Only **recovery eligibility** and **cross-rung escalation** belong to the runner.
- **`mergeLedger` (`typing.ts`) and `mergedAttempts` (the agent fill tool) are the concrete deletion criteria** (plan §12 item 5). FEAT-034 is incomplete while any listed recovery wrapper remains.
- **Backward compatibility is mandatory** (memory → General; plan §8). Audit/report readers accept legacy `AttemptRecord` artifacts and normalize them on read. **No old run directory is rewritten.**
- **`strategy` and `axis` keep their Wave 1 meanings** (plan §10). This feature re-groups data that already exists; it does not redefine the axes.
- **No website-specific logic** (memory → General). Every entry condition is structural: observed value flow, focus, ARIA relationships, what the widget offered, and the runner's own accounting. A site name in a rung, an entry condition, or a plan builder is a bug.
- **The secret path is unchanged.** `allowEscalation: false` builds a one-rung plan, still commits blind, still never reads back, and contributes no evidence to any ledger.

### Explicitly out of scope

Anything FEAT-031 shipped (the WHERE/WHAT/HOW axes, `AttemptRecord.axis`, the combobox driver family, query shaping, the open-probe stage, `(code, cause)` failure templates, batch partial progress, the `editee` disclosure) is substrate, not scope. FEAT-032's gauntlet and message catalog, FEAT-033's obstruction protocol, and FEAT-037's shadow/virtualized capabilities are dependencies whose capabilities are **not** re-specified here — FEAT-034 only has to make its `Rung` shape able to express FEAT-033's stage (entry condition, one bounded attempt, mandatory drive-or-dismiss), which Wave 1's open probe already established.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does **not** exist, and plan §4 states plainly that **no new relational schema and no Data Modeller pass is needed for this plan**. There are therefore **no tables, no columns, no migrations, no indexes and no foreign keys in this feature**. Everything below is a **run-artifact / ledger contract shape**: TypeScript types inside `packages/core`, one serialized `details.attempted` projection recorded per call in `tool-calls.jsonl`, and the reader that normalizes the legacy shape of the same field. Plan §4 gives only the conceptual `EscalationPlan` / `Rung` / `RungVerdict`; the granular shapes are designed here.

### Entities & Attributes

**`InteractionFamily`** — a closed union naming the one plan each family owns. This is the unit plan §11 counts ("1 runner + 1 plan per family").

`'text' | 'combobox' | 'date' | 'option' | 'field' | 'click'`. The first four extend `WidgetFamily` (`packages/core/src/widgets/types.ts:13`) with the engine's plain-text branch; `'field'` is the agent tool's top-level fill (resolve → drive → re-resolve); `'click'` is `browser_click`. The two agent-side families are **declared in `packages/agent`** and executed by the core runner — see the dependency-direction constraint.

**`EscalationPlan<TValue>`** — the ordered, inspectable recovery policy for one operation. Built by a **pure builder** from the family's declared rung templates plus the facts already read before execution (detected drivers, control shape, whether the caller holds a baseline observation). It is data: it contains no control flow, and reordering its `rungs` array reorders execution with no other edit.

- `family` (`InteractionFamily`) — NOT NULL. Exactly one exported builder per value; asserted by a completeness test.
- `operation` (`string`) — stable operation label recorded on the ledger, e.g. `fill-combobox`, `click`. NOT NULL.
- `rungs` (`readonly Rung<TValue>[]`) — NOT NULL, non-empty. **Order is the escalation order.**
- `budget` (`PlanBudget`) — NOT NULL. The single allowance the runner owns.
- `reacquire` (`(ref: string) => Promise<string | null>`, optional) — how the runner-owned port heals a stale ref. Injected, because "which live node is the control already identified" is a family-specific value decision (`engine.ts:reacquireTarget`) that must not move into the runner.
- `classify` (`(failure) => AttemptDisposition`, optional) — per-plan override of the shared `classifyFailure` table. Absent means the shared table, whose `details.reason === 'budget' | 'disabled'` override is preserved verbatim from Wave 1.

**`PlanBudget`** — what the runner enforces, in one place instead of six.

- `deadlineMs` (`number`) — absolute instant past which no rung starts. NOT NULL. `defaultWidgetBudget`'s 25 s ceiling is unchanged; the ≤ 4 s target is met by entry conditions, never by a smaller ceiling (FEAT-031 §2, deliberate).
- `maxActions` (`number`) — mutating port operations for the whole plan **including every sub-plan**. NOT NULL. Default 32, unchanged.
- `maxPagingSteps` (`number`) — carried through to drivers unchanged; paging is choreography inside a rung.
- `maxReacquisitions` (`number`) — declared stale-ref healing cap. Default 4, the value `MAX_REACQUISITIONS` holds today.

**`Rung<TValue>`** — one typed escalation step. The whole point of the feature: everything a recovery layer used to express as nesting is a field here.

- `id` (`string`) — NOT NULL, UNIQUE within the plan. Becomes the ledger's `strategy`, so Wave 1's names are preserved verbatim: `overtype`, `clear-then-type`, `native-setter`, `locate-editee`, `driver:<kind>`, `open-probe`, `fill`, `re-resolve-field-and-retry`, `query:<form>`, `re-acquire-target`, `re-acquire-and-click`. Never a site name.
- `axis` (`InteractionAxis`) — NOT NULL. `where` / `what` / `how`, reused unchanged from `packages/core/src/interaction/types.ts`.
- `entry` (`(evidence: RungEvidence, budget: BudgetState) => EntryDecision`) — NOT NULL. **Pure**: it reads only accumulated evidence and remaining budget, never the page. Page facts an entry condition needs (the control's date-shaped hint, whether a popup is linked, whether the caller supplied a baseline) are read once before the plan is built and passed into the builder. Purity is what makes fast-fail testable and free.
- `costCap` (`RungCost`) — NOT NULL. `{ maxActions: number; maxElapsedMs?: number }`. Declared, never inferred. Phase 3 refuses to _start_ a rung whose cap exceeds the remainder.
- `produces` (`readonly string[]`) — NOT NULL (may be empty). The evidence keys this rung can contribute (`editee`, `offered`, `chosen`, `committed`, `container`, `observedText`, `obstruction`, …). Declared so a later rung's entry condition cannot reference evidence no earlier rung produces — the same declared-not-inferred discipline FEAT-032 applies to `requiredDetails` / `capability`.
- `run` (`(ctx: RungContext<TValue>) => Promise<RungOutcome<TValue>>`) — NOT NULL. The action, executed through the runner-owned port. For an agent-declared plan this closes over **injected** core operations, which is how `packages/core` stays free of any adapter import.
- `cleanup` (`(ctx) => Promise<void>`, optional) — runs in a `finally` whenever the rung **entered**, never when it was skipped. This is the stage shape: Wave 1's open probe (one bounded attempt plus a mandatory dismiss) and FEAT-033's single bounded clearance are both expressible as a rung with `cleanup`, which is why obstruction landing first costs FEAT-034 one plan entry rather than a redesign.
- `backoffMs` (`number`, optional) — pause before this rung. The deadline governs whether the next rung may start **pause included**, preserving `attempt.ts`'s existing rule that waiting out a backoff only to be cut off mid-attempt spends the caller's time for nothing.
- `terminalOn` (`readonly string[]`, optional) — codes that end the plan immediately regardless of remaining rungs.

**`EntryDecision`** — a two-arm discriminated union. `{ enter: true; evidence: readonly string[] }` names the evidence keys that satisfied the condition; `{ enter: false; unmet: string }` names the **one** unmet condition. `unmet` is a fixed vocabulary of structural strings (`no-baseline-observation`, `control-not-empty`, `editee-located`, `previous-form-offered-candidates`, `driver-answered-definitively`, `semantics-disagree`, `insufficient-remaining-budget`, `deadline-expired`, `no-replacement-signal`) — **never page text**, so it is safe to log verbatim (plan §10, same reasoning as FEAT-033's `ObstructionKind`).

**`RungVerdict`** — a **discriminated union** on `kind`, and the replacement for `AttemptRecord`. Its discipline is the point: an impossible field is not merely unset, it is absent from the type.

- `{ kind: 'succeeded'; ordinal; rungId; axis; entryEvidence; chargedActions; remainingActions; elapsedMs; evidence }` — carries what the rung learned. **No `errorCode` key exists on this arm** (not `null` — absent).
- `{ kind: 'failed'; ordinal; rungId; axis; entryEvidence; chargedActions; remainingActions; elapsedMs; errorCode; cause?; detail? }` — `errorCode` is a **stable** code from the frozen code set FEAT-032 snapshots. `cause` is the Wave 1 internal `InteractionFailureCause`, never serialized to the model.
- `{ kind: 'skipped'; ordinal; rungId; axis; unmet }` — carries the **unmet entry condition** and nothing else. A skipped rung spent nothing, so it has no `chargedActions`, no `elapsedMs`, and no `errorCode`.

Shared attribute meanings: `ordinal` (`number`, 1-based across the whole ledger including sub-plans, so the sequence reads in the order it happened); `rungId` → serialized as `strategy`, Wave 1 meaning; `axis` → Wave 1 meaning; `entryEvidence` (bounded, sanitized at the agent seam like every other page-derived detail); `chargedActions` (what the runner-owned port actually counted, not a rung count); `remainingActions` (what was left after this rung — this is what makes "which axis spent the budget?" answerable).

**`EscalationLedger`** — `{ operation; family; verdicts: readonly RungVerdict[]; chargedActions; elapsedMs; remainingActions }`. The sequence of verdicts **is** the attempt ledger; Wave 1's `AttemptRecord.axis` is the on-ramp, so this is a re-grouping of data that already exists.

**`AttemptRecord` / `AttemptLedger`** (`packages/core/src/interaction/types.ts`) — **retained**, demoted to the **legacy read shape**. No producer emits it after TASK-011; every reader still accepts it.

**Serialized `details.attempted[]`** — the one durable projection, snake_cased to match every other tool `details` payload:

| Key                                                  | Present on        | Notes                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `ordinal`                                            | all               | 1-based                                          |
| `strategy`                                           | all               | `rung.id`, Wave 1 meaning                        |
| `axis`                                               | all               | `where` / `what` / `how`                         |
| `verdict`                                            | all               | `succeeded` / `failed` / `skipped`               |
| `entry_evidence`                                     | succeeded, failed | bounded key list                                 |
| `charged_actions`, `remaining_actions`, `elapsed_ms` | succeeded, failed | —                                                |
| `error_code`                                         | **failed only**   | stable code; **absent**, never `null`, elsewhere |
| `detail`                                             | failed            | one short observed clause                        |
| `unmet`                                              | **skipped only**  | fixed structural vocabulary                      |

### Relationships

- One **`EscalationPlan`** has many ordered **`Rung`s** (1:N by array position; position _is_ the relationship). Running the plan produces one **`RungVerdict`** per rung — every rung yields a verdict, including the skipped ones, which is what makes "why did this rung not run?" answerable at all.
- One **`EscalationLedger`** aggregates N `RungVerdict`s (1:N). It is a projection of the executed plan, not a parallel record.
- A **`Rung`'s** body may run a **sub-plan through the same runner**, sharing the parent's `PlanBudget`, deadline, and ledger. Sub-plan verdicts append to the parent ledger in place, so nesting produces an ordered sequence **by construction** — this is precisely what deletes `mergeLedger` (typing) and `mergedAttempts` (the agent fill tool) rather than reimplementing them. A rung may **never** call a different retry runner.
- `Rung.entry` N:1 the evidence keys declared by earlier rungs' `produces` in the same plan (validated statically by a plan-shape test).
- `RungVerdict{kind:'failed'}.errorCode` N:1 the frozen code set FEAT-032 snapshots, and N:1 a registered `MessageTemplate` via `(surface, code, cause)`.
- Legacy `AttemptRecord` 1:1 `RungVerdict` via `normalizeAttemptArtifact`: `errorCode === null` → `succeeded`, otherwise → `failed`. `skipped` has no legacy counterpart, which is exactly the information the old shape could not carry.

### Indexes & Constraints

- **UNIQUE `Rung.id` within a plan** — a duplicate makes the ledger ambiguous about which rung a verdict belongs to.
- **UNIQUE `EscalationPlan.family`** across exported builders — exactly one plan per interaction family, asserted by a completeness test. This is plan §11's "1 runner + 1 plan per family" made mechanical.
- **Exactly one escalation runner** in `packages/*/src` — enforced in `packages/core/tests/boundary-rules.spec.ts` alongside its existing "keeps candidate ranking to exactly one implementation" rule.
- **Referential integrity on evidence** — every key an `entry` reads appears in some earlier rung's `produces`.
- **Totality of `axis` and `costCap`** — every rung declares both; there is no default axis and no unbounded rung.
- **Prohibited: `error_code: null` inside an overall failure.** FEAT-032 characterizes the legacy case so the gate can observe it; FEAT-034 **flips that characterization** into a tested prohibition when this ledger lands (plan §9).
- **Reader totality** — `normalizeAttemptArtifact` is total over the legacy shape and never throws; a malformed record degrades to a `failed` verdict with the record's own code rather than failing the read.
- **No run-artifact rewrite** — normalization happens on read only. Asserted with a checked-in legacy run-directory fixture whose bytes must not change.

- **FEAT-032 (Widget Gauntlet & Copy-Hygiene Harness)** — the authoritative mutating-action counter, the registry-driven per-fixture reporting, the message catalog, and the legacy `errorCode: null` characterization this feature flips.

- **The adapter contract matrices** — `packages/agent/tests/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-tools.spec.ts`, `browser-tools.spec.ts`, and `e2e/agent-browser.spec.ts` — are the second half of the entry gate.

- **No dependency on FEAT-035 or FEAT-036.** Plan row order places both after this feature.

### TASK-002: `runEscalationPlan` — the runner, the plan/rung/verdict contract, and the runner-owned port

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `packages/core/src/interaction/escalation.ts` with the shapes from §2 and `runEscalationPlan`. Per rung, in order: (1) evaluate the **pure** `rung.entry(evidence, budgetState)`; on `{enter:false, unmet}` record a `skipped` verdict and continue; (2) execute `rung.run` through the **runner-owned port wrapper**, which counts every mutating action (`click`, `fill`, `clear`, `type`, `press`, scroll) and every read, and heals a stale ref via the plan's injected `reacquire`, capped by `budget.maxReacquisitions`; (3) record a `succeeded` or `failed` verdict carrying `entryEvidence`, `elapsedMs`, `chargedActions`, `remainingActions`; (4) run `rung.cleanup` in a `finally` **only when the rung entered**; (5) stop on a terminal disposition (shared `classifyFailure` table or `rung.terminalOn`), on the deadline including the backoff pause, or when rungs run out. Accept an optional parent context so a rung body can run a **sub-plan on the same budget, deadline, and ledger**, appending verdicts in place. **In this phase the runner counts but does not enforce**: `remainingActions` is recorded, and every existing budget check stays exactly where it is, so no budget boundary moves. Export `toLegacyLedger(EscalationLedger): AttemptLedger` producing byte-identical Wave 1 records (`attempt`, `strategy = rung.id`, `axis`, `errorCode` — `null` on success, `elapsedMs`, `detail`), with `skipped` verdicts omitted because Wave 1 could not represent them. Move `classifyFailure` / `TRANSIENT_CODES` / `TERMINAL_CODES` here unchanged and re-export from `attempt.ts`. **No call sites yet** — `withAttempts` remains in use.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. This feature adds no user-facing surface, no CLI flag, no preference, and no consent decision.
- **Error Handling**: Stable error codes are **unchanged** — FEAT-034 changes which record carries a code, never the codes or the wording. Wave 1's `(code, cause)` templates and FEAT-032's catalog remain the single source of model-visible text. `classifyFailure`'s `details.reason === 'budget' | 'disabled'` override is preserved verbatim: `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED` is in `TRANSIENT_CODES`, so a budget-exhausted one is terminal _only_ by that key, and losing it would loop budget failures to the rung bound. An unrecognised code stays **terminal by default**. `browserFailure`'s re-throw of unrecognised errors still escapes the runner rather than being retried blindly. Custom `Error` subclasses are untouched; nothing is silently swallowed.
- **Logging**: The ledger becomes a projection of the executed plan in the sanitized `tool-calls.jsonl` record (plan §10). `strategy` and `axis` keep their Wave 1 meanings; `verdict`, `entry_evidence`, `charged_actions`, and `remaining_actions` make "why did this rung run?" and "which axis spent the budget?" answerable directly from the artifact. `unmet` is a fixed structural vocabulary carrying no page text and is safe to log verbatim; `entry_evidence` is page-derived, bounded, and passes the same sanitizer as every other observation field at the agent seam. Structured Pino logging is unchanged and no new sink is added.
- **Security**: The secret path is preserved by construction — `allowEscalation: false` builds a one-rung plan that commits blind, performs no readback, and contributes **no evidence** to any verdict, so no secret-derived value can reach a ledger, a failure detail, or a log. Asserted by a dedicated test. Sanitization, budgets, and audit enforcement stay outside prompt text.
- **Dependency direction**: `packages/core` exports the runner and the plan types; `packages/agent` declares the `field` and `click` plans and injects core operations into their rung bodies. `packages/core` never imports `@yantra/agent`, enforced by the existing `boundary-rules.spec.ts` rule.
- **Backward compatibility**: Audit and report readers normalize legacy `AttemptRecord` artifacts on read (TASK-011). **No old run directory is rewritten**, per memory's run-artifact compatibility rule. User-owned workflow YAML is untouched; the deterministic replay path's behavior is unchanged and remains hard zero-LLM.
- **No website-specific logic**: every entry condition, rung id, and evidence key is structural. `boundary-rules.spec.ts`'s existing website-specific-logic rule already covers the new modules by path.
- **Testing**: Vitest, AAA behavior tests, injected clocks and ports, mocks only at external boundaries; core suites tagged `@no-LLM` and run on macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu. Artifact assertions read bytes through an explicit UTF-8 decoder (plan §9).
